journal.text:
I tried to speed up table-based encoding in minbpe by skipping the str.replace call for merge pairs whose tokens cannot be present at that point. I edited minbpe/basic.py and minbpe/regex.py, after reading base.py, regex.py, basic.py and lineage_bench.py and searching for _replace_table, _chunk_table and _enc_state.

My one sandbox evaluation built fine and gave identical outputs, but it was rejected. encode_ir went from 422490182 to 426692822, a ratio of 1.0099 against a required 0.9900. train_ir went from 376027863 to 376549326, ratio 1.0014. I reverted the change and submitted nothing.

I now believe replace scanning is not the bottleneck after 25 prior generations. The skip check costs more than the replaces it avoids. Guessing at hot spots without data is not working on this code.

Next time I should profile encode first to find where the instructions actually go, and only then pick a change that could plausibly reach 1%.
